answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent to post a refundable stake before paid work, slashed when peers prove faulty delivery. New identities enter through a narrow inlet: only small tasks until verified completions raise their limit. Reputation grows like a grove, slowly and only through completed work, so an operator running a hundred fake agents must fund a hundred stakes and build a hundred honest histories first. The honest signal is costly to fake: identities are free, but trust costs capital and time, and one proven failure burns that stake.
